(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better. Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better. Expected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better. Of the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better. The mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better. Client wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better. Input tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Lower is better. Measured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better.

Model
Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better. · of 2,069 pairs
(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better. · 0–100

Expected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better. · error, points

Of the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better. · caught · false alarms

The mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better. · 0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under it

Client wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better. · median, p90 under it

Input tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Lower is better. · $ per 1,000 pairs

Measured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better. · s per 1,000 pairs

Expected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better. · error, points

Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better. · of 2,069 pairs

Of the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better. · caught · false alarms

The mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Client wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Model

Of the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better. · caught · false alarms
(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better. · 0–100
Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better. · of 2,069 pairs

Expected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better. · error, points

The mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better. · 0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under it

Client wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better. · median, p90 under it

Input tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Lower is better. · $ per 1,000 pairs

Measured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better. · s per 1,000 pairs

Model

The mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better. · 0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under it
(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better. · 0–100
Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better. · of 2,069 pairs

Expected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better. · error, points

Of the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better. · caught · false alarms

Client wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better. · median, p90 under it

Input tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Lower is better. · $ per 1,000 pairs

Measured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better. · s per 1,000 pairs

head: The place by the chosen measure among the models in view, 1, 2, 3; a model without that measure is listed after them with –.
Model

Client wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better. · median, p90 under it
(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better. · 0–100
Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better. · of 2,069 pairs

Expected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better. · error, points

Of the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better. · caught · false alarms

The mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better. · 0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under it

Input tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Lower is better. · $ per 1,000 pairs

Measured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better. · s per 1,000 pairs

head: The place by the chosen measure among the models in view, 1, 2, 3; a model without that measure is listed after them with –.
Model

Input tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Lower is better. · $ per 1,000 pairs
(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better. · 0–100
Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better. · of 2,069 pairs

Expected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better. · error, points

Of the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better. · caught · false alarms

The mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better. · 0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under it

Client wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Runs at different concurrency are not speeds under the same load, and neither are runs on different hardware (our RTX PRO 6000, a DGX Spark or the maker's API, named in the model's box), even at the same concurrency. Lower is better. · median, p90 under it

Measured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better. · s per 1,000 pairs

Measured wall time of the whole run on the row's own GPU, named under the value (our RTX PRO 6000 or a DGX Spark), model load excluded, over all the pairs it answered, per 1,000 pairs: a rate, not API dollars. Seconds on different hardware are not like for like, even at the same requests in flight. Lower is better. · s per 1,000 pairs
(accuracy − 1/3) / (2/3) × 100: 0 = one of the three labels at random on every pair, 100 = every pair right; below chance reads below 0. Higher is better. · 0–100
Correct recorded labels out of all 2,069 pairs; a reply without a usable label counts wrong. Higher is better. · of 2,069 pairs

Expected calibration error over 10 equal-width bins of the chosen label's probability, in points. Only where the run gives option probabilities: it is not a confidence, and none is derived for chat models. Lower is better. · error, points

Of the 329 pairs whose summary states a conflicting answer, the share labelled so (recall); under it, false alarms: 'conflicting' given on the 1,740 pairs that state the answer or give none. An invalid reply counts as missed, never as a correct rejection. Higher is better. · caught · false alarms

The mean over all 2,069 pairs of 50 × (1 + c − (p − c)²), p the probability the run gave its chosen label and c 1 when that label is right: accuracy with a penalty for confident mistakes, the same formula as Logic & Math's. Under it, the chosen-answer Brier score, the mean of (p − c)², lower is better. Only where the run gives option probabilities: none for chat models. Higher is better. · 0–100 · chosen-answer Brier under it

Client wall time per request: the median, the 90th percentile under it, and how many requests ran at once. Lower is better. · median, p90 under it

Input tokens billed × the maker's list price, per 1,000 pairs (the price, its source and date in the model's box); a list price, not an invoice. A subscription run (no per-use charge) shows its tokens at the list price, marked 'estimated: subscription'. Not verified: no list price of that model at that date could be checked; never a zero. Open · 31B

MachinePulseAI/Karpo Decision 31B@d69cdd57, its card's karpo-decision package (machinepulse-ai/karpo-decision@ac40d399) System One server, BF16, on one RTX PRO 6000 (ours), self-hosted; one question per request, 1 request at a time (latency not comparable across different concurrency); before the run, 3 published-cohort pairs were sent in test requests whose outputs were not kept, so their scored rows come from a later request

forms: each no-code pair asked again: 'control' the scored request unchanged; 'order1', 'order2' the three options in two different changed orders (the same orders for every model); 'names' the options' keys replaced by plain letters in reverse; 'dontknow' the not-stated option reworded. Question, reference answer and text never change. Exception: where a model's server reorders options itself (its 'applicability' says so), a form reaches the model as that order, not as sent
applicability: per model and form, set only where the form did not reach the model as defined; such a cell is not comparable with other models' cells, and its figures are observations only
flip rate: share of pairs whose chosen option, by meaning, differs from the model's own scored Answer Check run
mean confidence change: mean absolute change in the probability the model gives its scored run's pick

control: the scored request repeated unchanged on the consistency load, read against the model's scored run: a difference can come from the setup as well as from repetition (see a model's note); the other forms are read against it
model echo checked: true when every reply named the same model as the scored run's replies; false when the model's replies name none, so the load's pinned weights are the identity evidence

scope: our-GPU decision models only, each on the same pinned weights and server software as its scored run unless its note says otherwise, one request at a time; separate from every score, the ranking and the Decision Index
